key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst coupled with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger greatly boosts solar-driven CO2-to-CO/CH4 conversion while adding a carbon-negative capture step.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable device-material strategy that combines catalyst design and biological CO2 uptake to improve photocatalytic carbon conversion efficiency.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta for charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 reduction with no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment will depend on maintaining microalgae viability and reactor compatibility under real operating conditions, not just short-term lab performance.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
